Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Windows Defender Offline scan trigger — GreatXML vulnerability precondition · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] GreatXML BitLocker Bypass — unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml dropped on recovery partition
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] User-initiated reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (GreatXML trigger) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
GreatXML BitLocker Bypass — unattend.xml / ReAgent.xml dropped on recovery partition AIWeaponization High
Detects file writes of the two specific XML artefacts the GreatXML PoC requires: an `unattend.xml` at the root of a non-system volume (the recovery partition) and/or a `ReAgent.xml` under a `\Recovery\WindowsRE\` path on a volume other than the OS install. The legitimate ReAgent.xml lives in `C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\`; writes elsewhere are the exploit staging the WinRE boot. Rationale: Anchors on the two exact filenames the article names (`unattend.xml`, `Recovery/WindowsRE/ReAgent.xml`) and carves out their legitimate Windows locations (`C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\` for ReAgent, `C:\Windows\Panther\`/`Sysprep\` for unattend). A write outside those canonical paths plus excluding TrustedInstaller/Defender/reagentc as initiator yields very high fidelity because no normal Windows component writes these names to a recovery-partition path.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MDT/SCCM task-sequence staging an OS image and dropping unattend.xml to a custom path on a USB/PXE volume
  • OEM imaging tools (Dell Image Assist, Lenovo Smart Standby) writing OEM recovery configuration
  • IT admin manually customising WinRE via `reagentc /setreimage` workflow which can copy ReAgent.xml
  • Backup software (Veeam, Macrium) restoring system-state including recovery partition contents
  • Researcher / penetration-tester intentionally reproducing the GreatXML PoC on a test host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft Deployment Toolkit\", @"\SMSTSWiz\", @"\osdcloud\") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("DISM.exe","setup.exe","OSDSetupHook.exe","TSManager.exe","smsts.exe"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the InitiatingProcess tree and the user account. Confirm whether the host has an active deployment / imaging task running (check SCCM/MDT logs) or whether the initiating process is a known imaging tool. Note whether the recovery partition was just mounted (look for nearby `diskpart`, `mountvol`, or `assign letter=` activity). Step 2 — Contain: if no legitimate imaging context, isolate the host via MDE Live Response and block the user from initiating a reboot. Preserve the recovery partition contents — copy the two XML files for IR. Do NOT let the host reboot until reviewed; a Shift+Restart finishes the exploit. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the same user/host for prior `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or `Start-MpWDOScan` (the prerequisite), nearby `reagentc.exe /boottore` or `shutdown.exe /r /o` (the trigger), and look across the fleet for other hosts that received the same two file names from the same source process or share / IP.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FileName =~ "ReAgent.xml"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\Recovery"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Recovery"
            and FolderPath has @"\Recovery\WindowsRE")
     or (FileName =~ "unattend.xml"
            and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
            and FolderPath !contains @"\Panther\"
            and FolderPath !contains @"\Sysprep\")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","reagentc.exe","wuauclt.exe","TiWorker.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated" or EventType =~ "FileModified" or EventType =~ "FileRenamed"
| where (TargetFileName =~ "ReAgent.xml"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\Recovery"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Recovery"
            and TargetFilePath has @"\Recovery\WindowsRE")
     or (TargetFileName =~ "unattend.xml"
            and TargetFilePath !startswith @"C:\Windows\"
            and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Panther\"
            and TargetFilePath !contains @"\Sysprep\")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsMpEng.exe","MpCmdRun.exe","reagentc.exe","wuauclt.exe","TiWorker.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, EventType,
          ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GreatXML BitLocker Bypass - Recovery Partition XML Drop
id: 7a1e3f8c-b9d2-4a51-9e6f-2c4b8d9a1e30
description: Detects creation of unattend.xml or ReAgent.xml outside their canonical Windows paths - the staging step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass that drops these files onto the recovery partition before a WinRE boot.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.005
  - attack.t1112
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  reagent_xml:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\Recovery\WindowsRE\ReAgent.xml'
  reagent_xml_filter:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\Recovery\'
      - 'C:\Recovery\'
  unattend_xml:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\unattend.xml'
  unattend_xml_filter:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - 'C:\Windows\'
      - '\Panther\'
      - '\Sysprep\'
  benign_writer:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\MpCmdRun.exe'
      - '\reagentc.exe'
      - '\TiWorker.exe'
  condition: ((reagent_xml and not reagent_xml_filter) or (unattend_xml and not unattend_xml_filter)) and not benign_writer
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\ReAgent.xml OR *\\recovery\\windowsre\\reagent.xml) OR (@TargetFilename:(*\\unattend.xml OR *\\Unattend.xml OR *\\UNATTEND.XML) AND -@TargetFilename:(*\\Windows\\* OR *\\Panther\\* OR *\\Sysprep\\*))) AND -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\MsMpEng.exe OR *\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\reagentc.exe OR *\\TiWorker.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| (regex("(?i)\\\\Recovery\\\\WindowsRE\\\\ReAgent\\.xml$", field=TargetFileName) AND NOT regex("(?i)^C:\\\\(Windows\\\\System32\\\\Recovery|Recovery)\\\\", field=TargetFileName)) OR (regex("(?i)\\\\unattend\\.xml$", field=TargetFileName) AND NOT regex("(?i)\\\\(Windows|Panther|Sysprep)\\\\", field=TargetFileName))
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_id) as process_id values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\System32\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Recovery\\*") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*") OR (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Panther\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Sysprep\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name,"(?i)(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_id) as process_id values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="ReAgent.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\System32\\Recovery\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Recovery\\*") AND Filesystem.file_path="*\\Recovery\\WindowsRE\\*") OR (Filesystem.file_name="unattend.xml" AND NOT (Filesystem.file_path="C:\\Windows\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Panther\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Sysprep\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_name,"(?i)(TrustedInstaller|MsMpEng|MpCmdRun|reagentc|TiWorker)\.exe$")
User-initiated reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (GreatXML trigger) AIExploitation Medium
Detects the WinRE-boot trigger the GreatXML PoC requires: either `reagentc.exe /boottore` programmatically, or `shutdown.exe /r /o` (the CLI equivalent of Shift+Restart). Pair with UC1 (recovery-partition XML drop) on the same host to confirm the bypass attempt. Rationale: `reagentc.exe /boottore` and `shutdown.exe /r /o` are the only two CLI paths to a WinRE boot; both are uncommon outside of IT-helpdesk troubleshooting and OS upgrade flows. Pairs with UC1 - a recovery-partition XML drop followed within minutes by a WinRE-boot trigger from the same host is the full GreatXML chain.
ATT&CKT1542.005 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk technician walking a user through Advanced Startup to repair boot issues
  • Windows Update / feature update flows occasionally invoke `reagentc` during servicing
  • SCCM / Intune remediation scripts that schedule a reboot to recovery for repair
  • Power user troubleshooting their own machine via Settings -> Recovery -> Restart now
  • Hardware vendor diagnostics tools (Dell SupportAssist, Lenovo Vantage) booting to recovery
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","UsoClient.exe","SupportAssistAgent.exe","VantageService.exe") or InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "services.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the parent-process chain for the reboot command. Helpdesk-driven recovery boots usually come from `explorer.exe` or `mmc.exe` via Settings; scripted attacker chains often come from `cmd.exe`/`powershell.exe` or an SSH/RDP session. Cross-check whether the user has an open helpdesk ticket. Step 2 — Contain: if the host has UC1 (recovery-partition XML write) inside the prior 60 minutes, treat as confirmed GreatXML chain - block the reboot through your EDR/MDM rebooting policy and isolate the host before WinRE is reached. Step 3 — Hunt: search for `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or `Start-MpWDOScan` on the same host in the prior 30 days (the precondition) and pivot the user identity across other endpoints for the same chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "reagentc.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/boottore","-boottore","boottore"))
     or (FileName =~ "shutdown.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/o" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/r","/g"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\reagentc.exe" and (CommandLine has_any ("/boottore","-boottore","boottore")))
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\shutdown.exe" and CommandLine has "/o" and CommandLine has_any ("/r","/g"))
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Reboot to Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) - GreatXML Trigger
id: 8b2f4a9d-c0e3-4b62-af70-3d5c9e0b2f41
description: Detects the CLI invocations that boot a Windows host into WinRE - the trigger step of the GreatXML BitLocker bypass after unattend.xml and ReAgent.xml have been staged on the recovery partition.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1542.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  reagentc:
    Image|endswith: '\reagentc.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/boottore'
      - '-boottore'
      - 'boottore'
  shutdown_to_recovery:
    Image|endswith: '\shutdown.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '/o'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/o'
  shutdown_reboot_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/r'
      - '/g'
  condition: reagentc or (shutdown_to_recovery and shutdown_reboot_flag)
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\reagentc.exe OR *\\ReAgentC.exe OR *\\REAGENTC.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*boottore* OR *BootToRE* OR *BOOTTORE*)) OR (@Image:(*\\shutdown.exe OR *\\Shutdown.exe OR *\\SHUTDOWN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*\/o* OR *-o*) AND @CommandLine:(*\/r* OR *\/g*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\reagentc\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/boottore/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\shutdown\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\s\/o\b/i AND CommandLine=/\s\/(r|g)\b/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*boottore*" OR Processes.process="*BootToRE*")) OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND (Processes.process="*/r*" OR Processes.process="*/g*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="reagentc.exe" AND (Processes.process="*boottore*" OR Processes.process="*BootToRE*")) OR (Processes.process_name="shutdown.exe" AND Processes.process="*/o*" AND (Processes.process="*/r*" OR Processes.process="*/g*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
Windows Defender Offline scan trigger — GreatXML vulnerability precondition AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts for hosts that initiated a Windows Defender Offline scan via `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` or PowerShell `Start-MpWDOScan`. Per the article, this action puts the host into the state that makes the GreatXML bypass exploitable; surfacing it gives an audit of which endpoints are now susceptible to recovery-partition XML staging. Rationale: Article quote: 'If you ever attempted to use Windows Defender Offline Scan, you're automatically vulnerable to a BitLocker bypass.' The two canonical ways to invoke WDO are `MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot` and the `Start-MpWDOScan` PowerShell cmdlet - both are uncommon in fleet baselines and worth tracking as an exposure-audit hunt rather than an alert.
ATT&CKT1518.001 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Helpdesk running WDO scan to remediate a stubborn malware detection
  • User-initiated WDO scan via Windows Security UI as part of a deep-scan workflow
  • Endpoint-management policy that schedules periodic WDO scans
  • IR analyst running WDO as part of incident triage on a suspected-compromised host
  • Vendor-driven malware-cleanup recommendations that suggest running WDO
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe","MsMpEng.exe","SenseIR.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName == "services.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm whether the WDO invocation aligns with a known IT-driven scan ticket or user-initiated UI action. The parent process tells you - `services.exe` -> scheduled task, `explorer.exe` -> user UI, scripted parents are unusual. Step 2 — Audit: flag the host as 'GreatXML-vulnerable' in your asset inventory and prioritise it for the next patch cycle / WinRE reset (`reagentc /disable` then `/enable`). Until then, monitor for UC1 + UC2 chain on that host. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot the user across other endpoints for similar WDO invocations and look for clusters that suggest an attacker priming many hosts at once.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-WDOBoot","WDOBoot"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Invocations = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 8)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName
| order by LastSeen desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\MpCmdRun.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("-WDOBoot","WDOBoot"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" and CommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
     or (NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe" and CommandLine has "Start-MpWDOScan")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Invocations = count(),
            SampleCmd = any(CommandLine)
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Windows Defender Offline Scan Triggered - GreatXML Vulnerability Precondition
id: 9c3a5b0e-d1f4-4c73-b081-4e6d0f1c3a52
description: Surfaces hosts that have initiated a Windows Defender Offline scan via MpCmdRun.exe -WDOBoot or PowerShell Start-MpWDOScan. The article notes that any host which has run WDO is automatically susceptible to the GreatXML BitLocker bypass.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-greatxml-exploit-bypasses-windows.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1518.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  mpcmdrun:
    Image|endswith: '\MpCmdRun.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'WDOBoot'
  powershell_cmdlet:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'Start-MpWDOScan'
  condition: mpcmdrun or powershell_cmdlet
level: low
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\MpCmdRun.exe OR *\\mpcmdrun.exe OR *\\MPCMDRUN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*WDOBoot* OR *wdoboot* OR *WDOBOOT*)) OR (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*Start-MpWDOScan* OR *start-mpwdoscan*)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\MpCmdRun\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/WDOBoot/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Start-MpWDOScan/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName], function=count(), function=min(@timestamp))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" AND Processes.process="*WDOBoot*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="MpCmdRun.exe" AND Processes.process="*WDOBoot*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*Start-MpWDOScan*") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"\$$")
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45585")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45585")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-45585")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d05
status: experimental
description: |
    User-driven consent to a third-party OAuth application — illicit-
    consent attack precursor. Pair with first-time-seen-app heuristic
    in your SIEM for higher fidelity.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1528/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1528
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs
detection:
    selection:
        OperationName: 'Consent to application'
        Result: 'success'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate first-time SaaS app onboarding
level: medium
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Add delegated permission grant")
    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

CodeIgniter4 ext_in bypass: HTTP upload with image MIME and executable file extension AIDelivery High
Detects CVE-2026-48062 exploitation at the wire: an HTTP POST to a web app declares an image/* Content-Type but the uploaded filename ends in .php/.phar/.phtml/.phps. This is the exact validator bypass: ext_in trusts the MIME-guessed extension while the original filename retains the executable suffix. Rationale: Pinned to the article's exact mechanism: 'ext_in checked the MIME-derived guessed extension instead of the client-provided filename extension' — so the wire signature is image/* Content-Type paired with .php filename. ImWebSession's FileMimeType + FileName captures this directly; Web CIM's http_content_type covers Splunk. Cross-checked against CWE-434 (https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html) and OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html • https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1036.008 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CMS editor explicitly allowing PHP template upload (rare, legitimate admin path)
  • Bug-bounty/pentesters targeting the org's public web apps
  • Image-format converter tools naming output files with .php suffix because of misconfiguration
  • Developer uploading code via a forms-test endpoint in non-prod environments
  • Legacy web app where .php uploads to /uploads/ is intentional (poor design but real)
Suppression filter
| where not (SrcIpAddr in ("<known-admin-ip-1>","<known-admin-ip-2>")) | where not (Url has_any ("/admin/template-upload","/dev/code-upload"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the full POST — confirm Content-Type header, filename in Content-Disposition, response code (200 = file landed), and look at the request body's first bytes for GIF magic 47 49 46 38. Check whether the destination URL maps to a known CodeIgniter4 app and what package version it runs (vuln < 4.7.2). Contain: if response was 200, isolate the web host, take an inode-level snapshot of upload directories, deny public access to the upload path at the LB/WAF, and rotate any keys/credentials accessible to the web user. Hunt: pivot on src IP for prior reconnaissance and follow-up requests to the dropped filename; correlate with UC #4 (web worker spawn shell). Block src at perimeter and add a WAF rule rejecting image/* MIME with executable extensions org-wide.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where FileMimeType has_any ("image/gif","image/png","image/jpeg","image/jpg","image/webp")
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, FileName, FileMimeType, HttpResponseCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:(nginx OR apache OR iis OR cloudfront OR aws.elb) @http.method:POST (@http.request.headers.content-type:(image\/gif OR image\/png OR image\/jpeg OR image\/webp) OR @http.request.headers.Content-Type:(image\/gif OR image\/png OR image\/jpeg OR image\/webp)) (@http.url:(*upload*\.php* OR *upload*\.phar* OR *upload*\.phtml* OR *avatar*\.php*) OR @http.url_details.path:(*\.php OR *\.phar OR *\.phtml OR *\.phps))
WEB

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where Web.http_method="POST" AND Web.http_content_type IN ("image/gif","image/png","image/jpeg","image/jpg","image/webp") by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.http_user_agent Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where match(url, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)([\?&#]|$)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
CodeIgniter ext_in form validation rule failure surge against upload endpoints AIReconnaissance Medium
Surfaces reconnaissance/probing of the CVE-2026-48062 bypass by spotting application-log surges where CodeIgniter form-validation messages reference the ext_in / mime_in / is_image rules together with .php-family filenames. A burst from one source indicates an attacker iterating on validator bypasses. Rationale: Pinned to the article's named validator: 'The `ext_in` upload validation rule checked the MIME-derived guessed extension'. The article also names mime_in and is_image as adjacent rules in the example chain (`uploaded[avatar]|is_image[avatar]|mime_in[avatar,image/gif]|ext_in[avatar,gif]`), so logs mentioning these rules together with executable filenames are the strongest reconnaissance signal. Hunting tier because app logs are environment-specific; threshold of >3 is a probe-vs-typo cut. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/validation.html#rules-for-file-uploads
ATT&CKT1190 T1595.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate user typo'ing filenames in production (low-volume, unlikely > 3 hits)
  • QA/automated test suites validating the upload flow in staging environments
  • Developer running validator unit tests against a prod-like instance
  • Bulk-importer tool with extension-name field mistakes
  • Internal forms running in debug mode and emitting validation failures verbosely
Suppression filter
| where Computer !has "staging" and Computer !has "-qa-" | where ProcessName != "phpunit"
Response runbook
Triage: pull the Computer/host's last 24h of upload-endpoint requests — correlate failure timestamps with successful POSTs from the same source IP (the success after multiple failures is the bypass). Pull a sample SyslogMessage and the actual filename being uploaded. Contain: if same source IP got a 200 on a .php-suffixed file after the failures, isolate the web host (see UC #3). Apply WAF rule rejecting image MIME with .php-family extensions. Hunt: pivot on the source IP for related TTPs (other vuln classes, S3 enumeration, GitHub recon). Confirm CodeIgniter4 version is < 4.7.2 — if so, schedule emergency upgrade.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd","php")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("ext_in","mime_in","is_image","Validation failed")
| where SyslogMessage has_any (".php",".phar",".phtml",".phps","upload")
| summarize HitCount = count(), Rules = make_set(extract(@"(?i)(ext_in|mime_in|is_image)", 1, SyslogMessage)), Samples = make_list(SyslogMessage, 5), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer, HostIP, ProcessName
| where HitCount > 3
| order by HitCount desc
source:(php OR codeigniter OR nginx OR apache) (ext_in OR mime_in OR is_image OR "Validation failed") (\.php OR \.phar OR \.phtml OR \.phps OR upload)
APPLICATION
index=* sourcetype IN ("php_error","apache_error","nginx_error","codeigniter","php:errorlog") ("ext_in" OR "mime_in" OR "is_image") (".php" OR ".phar" OR ".phtml" OR "upload") | rex field=_raw "(?i)(?<rule>ext_in|mime_in|is_image)" | stats count, values(rule) as rules, values(_raw) as samples, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime by host, source | where count > 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Web server worker writes .php/.phar/.phtml file into public upload directory AIInstallation High
Detects the post-bypass file landing: a web-server worker (w3wp, php-fpm, httpd, nginx, php-cgi) writes a .php-family file into /public/, /uploads/, /writable/uploads/ or similar. Catches the polyglot drop regardless of MIME spoofing — once the .php file hits a web-accessible directory it's RCE-ready. Rationale: Pinned to the article's exact landing condition: 'save uploaded files using the original client filename: $file->move($path)' + 'store uploads in a web-accessible directory'. The article calls out writable/uploads as the SAFE path, so writes UNDER /public/, /webroot/, /uploads/, /avatars/ from a web-worker process are the smoking gun. File-extension regex is anchored to the exact PHP-family list the framework treats as executable. The Sysmon EID 11 angle covers Windows; ImFileEvent covers cross-platform. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://codeigniter.com/user_guide/libraries/uploaded_files.html#moving-files • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Composer/Symfony console deploying .php templates into public/ during release windows
  • Cache-warmer or template compiler writing compiled .php files into writable/cache
  • Bitnami/Plesk-style installers placing default PHP files under /public/ during provisioning
  • Legitimate CMS plugin writing PHP fragments to a public widget cache
  • Backup/restore tools rehydrating .php content into web-accessible directories
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","php artisan","--cache-warmup")) | where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName in ("deploy","composer","ci-runner"))
Response runbook
Triage: SHA256 the written file and search for it in DeviceFileEvents across the fleet (lateral spread of same artifact). Read the file's first 16 bytes — GIF magic `47 49 46 38` followed by `<?php` is a polyglot webshell. Pull DeviceProcessEvents for the writer process to see what HTTP request triggered the write. Contain: kill the web worker, quarantine the file, snapshot the upload directory, deny public read on the path at the LB. Rotate web-service credentials and DB creds reachable from PHP. Hunt: chain to UC #4 (web worker spawning shell) for confirmed exec; pivot on file SHA256 across the org; check git log of the CMS repo for unauthorized commits.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\public\", @"/public/", @"\uploads\", @"/uploads/", "writable", "avatars", "webroot")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc

DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where FolderPath has_any (@"\public\", @"/public/", @"\uploads\", @"/uploads/", "writable", "avatars", "webroot")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Web server worker writes PHP-family script into public upload directory
id: a2b8c4d6-e8f0-4a1b-9c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
description: Detects when a web-server worker process (w3wp/php-fpm/httpd/nginx/php-cgi) writes a .php, .phar, .phtml or .phps file into a public, uploads or writable directory. High-fidelity signal for CodeIgniter4 CVE-2026-48062 ext_in bypass and other unrestricted-upload web-shell drops.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx
  - https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
author: SOC Detection Team
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1036.008
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.php'
      - '.phar'
      - '.phtml'
      - '.phps'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\public\'
      - '\uploads\'
      - '\writable\'
      - '\avatars\'
      - '\webroot\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Composer/Symfony console deploying .php templates into public/ during release
  - In-app cache-warmer writing compiled .php templates to writable/cache
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE OR *\\php-fpm.exe OR *\\php-cgi.exe OR *\\php.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\nginx.exe)) (@TargetFilename:(*\\public\\*\.php* OR *\\public\\*\.phar* OR *\\uploads\\*\.php* OR *\\uploads\\*\.phar* OR *\\writable\\*\.php* OR *\\avatars\\*\.php* OR *\/public\/*\.php* OR *\/uploads\/*\.php* OR *\/writable\/uploads\/*\.php*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten | ContextImageFileName=/(w3wp|php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx)(\.exe)?$/i | TargetFileName=/\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$/i | regex("(public|uploads|writable|avatars|webroot)", field=TargetFileName) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(file_name, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$") | where match(file_path, "(?i)(public|uploads|writable|avatars|webroot)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action="created" AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(file_name, "(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$") | where match(file_path, "(?i)(public|uploads|writable|avatars|webroot)") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Web worker spawns interactive shell after PHP file write to upload directory (CodeIgniter4 CVE-2026-48062) AIActions on Objectives High
Time-window correlation: a web-server worker writes a .php/.phar/.phtml file into a public upload directory and then spawns an interactive shell or recon binary (bash, sh, cmd, powershell, whoami, id, curl, wget) within 10 minutes. This is the install→execute chain of the CVE-2026-48062 polyglot webshell bypass. Rationale: Pinned to the article's RCE chain: 'this may lead to arbitrary code execution' once the .php file is saved in a web-accessible directory. The high-fidelity signal is the temporal correlation between (a) the web worker writing the .php (left side, ImFileEvent / DeviceFileEvents) and (b) the same web worker spawning a shell or recon binary within minutes (right side, ImProcessCreate / DeviceProcessEvents). 10m window is generous enough to catch lazy attackers but tight enough to exclude unrelated noise. All Defender/Sentinel columns are canonical — TimeGenerated1/Timestamp1/FileName1 are auto-join-renames, not invented aliases. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2gr4-ppc7-7mhx • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/434.html
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CI/CD agent triggered by upload of a deploy package that legitimately runs setup scripts after extraction
  • Composer post-install hooks running shell commands shortly after vendor/ updates
  • Image-thumbnail generator legitimately calling curl/wget to fetch derived assets
  • System-management agent shelling out to whoami/id during health checks within the web-worker process tree (unusual but seen with some APM agents)
  • Web app with intentional curl-based webhooks fired from a freshly-written .php endpoint (rare and should be allowlisted)
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","php artisan","npm post")) | where not (ActingProcessName == "php-fpm" and TargetProcessName == "curl" and TargetProcessCommandLine has "thumbnailer")
Response runbook
Triage: get the SHA256 of the .php file and the full command line of the spawned shell — that command line typically reveals attacker intent (id; uname -a; curl http://...). Confirm the file was reachable via HTTP (check FolderPath maps to a documented webroot). Pull request logs for the dropped filename to find the source IP. Contain: kill all web-worker processes on the host, quarantine the file, segment the host from internal networks, snapshot for forensics, and rotate every credential the web user could read (DB, API keys, AWS IAM). Hunt: pivot on source IP across all web hosts; pivot on file SHA256 for fleet-wide spread; check for outbound C2 from the host in DeviceNetworkEvents in the same window; check CodeIgniter4 version on every public web host and patch < 4.7.2 immediately.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)\.(php|phar|phtml|phps)$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\public\", @"/public/", @"\uploads\", @"/uploads/", "writable", "avatars", "webroot")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","whoami","id","wget","curl")
) on DeviceId
| where Timestamp1 between (Timestamp .. Timestamp + 10m)
| project WriteTime=Timestamp, SpawnTime=Timestamp1, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second', Timestamp1, Timestamp), DeviceName, FolderPath, WrittenFile=FileName, WriterProc=InitiatingProcessFileName, SpawnedProc=FileName1, SpawnedCmd=ProcessCommandLine
| order by WriteTime desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("php","phar","phtml","phps")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\public\", @"/public/", @"/uploads/", @"\uploads\", "writable/uploads", "avatars", "webroot")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","apache2","php.exe","php-cgi.exe")
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","nginx","w3wp.exe","apache2","php.exe","php-cgi.exe")
    | where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","whoami","id","uname","wget","curl")
) on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated1 between (TimeGenerated .. TimeGenerated + 10m)
| project WriteTime=TimeGenerated, SpawnTime=TimeGenerated1, DelaySec=datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated1, TimeGenerated), DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by WriteTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.EXE OR *\\php-fpm.exe OR *\\php-cgi.exe OR *\\php.exe OR *\\httpd.exe OR *\\nginx.exe)) (@Image:(*\\bash OR *\\sh OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\curl.exe))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | ParentBaseFileName=/(w3wp\.exe|php-fpm|httpd|apache2|nginx|php-cgi\.exe|php\.exe)$/i | ImageFileName=/(bash|sh|cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|wscript\.exe|cscript\.exe|whoami|id|uname|wget|curl)(\.exe)?$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or SHA1 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68") or MD5 in~ ("22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["22b38dad7da097ea03aa28d0614164cd25fafeb1383dbc15047e34c8050f6f67", "078163d5c16f64caa5a14784323fd51451b8c831c73396b967b4e35e6879937b", "fe1033335a045c696c900d435119d210361966e2fb5cd1ba3382608cfa2c8e68"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
