Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Bun runtime fetched during npm/node install (Shai-Hulud TTP) · [LLM] package.json with postinstall containing curl/wget/powershell -enc or base64 written to disk · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — npm v12 delivers one of the biggest security improvements in years
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm/node spawning LOLBin child process during install (postinstall hook execution) · [LLM] node_modules postinstall writing to autostart / persistence paths · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound connection to known npm-supply-chain campaign IOCs from Node/npm/Bun · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Credential scanner (TruffleHog/gitleaks) spawned during npm install context · [LLM] Node/npm/Bun process reading SSH keys, npmrc or cloud credential files · [LLM] Cloud instance metadata service queried by Node/npm/Bun process · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
npm/node spawning LOLBin child process during install (postinstall hook execution) AIInstallation High
Hunts the canonical postinstall execution chain described in the article: npm/node/bun spawning a shell/script interpreter or download LOLBin during an install lifecycle. Pivots on parent being npm/node and the child being a non-build LOLBin or shell — the exact chain Nx s1ngularity's telemetry.js, the axios RAT dropper and Mini Shai-Hulud's Bun-puller all walked through. Rationale: Article anchors the entire v12 change on postinstall hooks spawning code as the user, with named campaigns (Nx s1ngularity telemetry.js, Mini Shai-Hulud Bun-puller, axios RAT dropper) all using this exact npm→shell/LOLBin chain. Parent-process pivot on node/npm + LOLBin child is the only universally shared TTP. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.004 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp rebuild legitimately invoking cl.exe/sh.exe for native modules (sharp, canvas, bcrypt, node-sass)
  • CI build agents running install scripts that legitimately curl assets
  • Developer running test suites that shell out via child_process.exec
  • Electron/postinstall hooks invoking PowerShell to set ACLs on installation
  • Husky git-hook installers that touch shell during install
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp", "prebuild-install", "node-pre-gyp") and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the full parent/child cmdline and check the package being installed (cwd usually node_modules/<pkg>); cross-check the package name against the npm advisories DB and Aikido Safe Chain feed. 2. Contain: isolate the host (Defender Live Response / EDR isolation), revoke the user's npm token + GitHub PAT + cloud creds reachable from the dev box, and remove the package from any private registry mirror that resolved it. 3. Hunt: pivot on the package name across all repos/devices in the last 30d (npm install lines in shell history, package-lock.json modifications); look for the same SHA256 child binary across the fleet and any outbound connection from node.exe to the IOC list in UC7.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm i ","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install","bun install","node-gyp rebuild","postinstall","preinstall")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","npm i ","npm ci","yarn install","pnpm install","bun install","node-gyp rebuild","postinstall","preinstall")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects npm/node/bun spawning a shell or download LOLBin during install lifecycle, the postinstall-hook attack chain described in Aikido npm v12 article.

tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\bun.exe'

  selection_child:

Bun runtime fetched during npm/node install (Shai-Hulud TTP) AIDelivery High
Detects the Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud signature: an npm package's install hook downloads or executes the Bun runtime from bun.sh / GitHub release URLs as a portable interpreter for credential-stealer payloads. Bun has near-zero legitimate use as a transient install-time dependency. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out Shai-Hulud (Nov 2025) and Mini Shai-Hulud (May 2026) as installing the Bun runtime during npm setup to run TruffleHog. Bun-as-install-time-tool from an npm/node parent context is a strong campaign-specific signal. Cross-checked against MITRE T1105 and the Shai-Hulud campaign writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.007 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer who intentionally uses Bun as a JS runtime/test runner (rare but real)
  • CI pipelines that document Bun as part of toolchain
  • Bun installation via Homebrew/winget by a developer not via npm postinstall
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm which npm package's lifecycle initiated the Bun download (look at parent npm install cwd / package-lock.json); compare against the package's published source on GitHub. 2. Contain: isolate the host, kill any active bun.exe + child processes, revoke any tokens (GitHub PAT, npm token, cloud) accessible from the workstation. 3. Hunt: pivot on the same package across all devs/CI in the last 60d; check GitHub audit log for any repos created or branches pushed by the user in the same window (Shai-Hulud writes secrets to public repos).
let BunDownloads = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
    | where RemoteUrl has_any ("bun.sh/install","github.com/oven-sh/bun","bun-install.sh")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl;
let BunExecs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node-gyp rebuild")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256;
BunDownloads
| union BunExecs
| order by Timestamp desc
let BunFromNetwork = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any ("bun.sh/install","github.com/oven-sh/bun","bun-install.sh")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent;
let BunExecs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "bun"
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
       or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node-gyp rebuild")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
BunFromNetwork
| union BunExecs
| order by TimeGenerated desc

  OR CommandLine=/bun\.sh\/install|github\.com\/oven-sh\/bun|bun-install\.sh/i
  OR DomainName=/^bun\.sh$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, DomainName], function=count())

Credential scanner (TruffleHog/gitleaks) spawned during npm install context AIActions on Objectives High
Catches the Shai-Hulud credential-harvesting stage: post-Bun-install execution of TruffleHog (or equivalent secret-scanner) parented to an npm/bun lifecycle. Legitimate dev use of TruffleHog runs from CI pipelines or developer terminals, not from npm postinstall. Rationale: Article cites Shai-Hulud running TruffleHog after installing Bun, scraping secrets and dumping them to public GitHub repos. TruffleHog with an npm/Bun parent is a fingerprint-quality signal — legitimate use almost never has that parent chain. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Husky pre-commit hook that calls gitleaks (parent will be git/sh, not npm install)
  • CI pipeline step that runs trufflehog after npm install in build script (allowlist CI hosts)
  • Developer manually piping `npm test && trufflehog` (rare; parent will be shell not npm)
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky","lint-staged","pre-commit") or DeviceName has "build-" or DeviceName has "ci-")
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the full cmdline incl. scan target paths (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc are the high-value targets); identify the originating npm package via cwd. 2. Contain: isolate the host, rotate every secret in any file the scanner had read access to (GitHub PATs, npm tokens, SSH keys, AWS creds, cloud-CLI sessions), and remove the offending package from any private registry. 3. Hunt: check GitHub audit log for new public repos created by the user in the last 7 days (Shai-Hulud exfil channel); search for outbound POSTs from the host to github.com/api or webhook.site at the time of the scan.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node-gyp rebuild")
| where FileName has_any ("trufflehog","gitleaks","detect-secrets","noseyparker")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git","gitleaks detect","detect-secrets scan")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node-gyp rebuild")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("trufflehog","gitleaks","detect-secrets","noseyparker")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem","trufflehog git","gitleaks detect","detect-secrets scan")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Node/npm/Bun process reading SSH keys, npmrc or cloud credential files AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the file-access stage of the Nx s1ngularity and Shai-Hulud postinstall stealers: the install-time process touches ~/.ssh, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, .env files or wallet directories that have no business being read during a package install. Rationale: Article: 'payload scans for tokens, SSH keys, and other goodies' and Nx s1ngularity 'scraped GitHub tokens, npm credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets'. Filtering DeviceFileEvents to credential-store paths with a node/npm/bun initiating process directly catches that step. Verified against MITRE T1552.001. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/004/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm CLI legitimately reading ~/.npmrc for auth token (high-frequency benign baseline — must keep but suppress when only .npmrc touched)
  • AWS SDK in a Node app reading ~/.aws/credentials during dev runtime (not during install)
  • VS Code remote extensions touching ~/.ssh known_hosts
  • Hashicorp Vault SDK reading kubeconfig in a build container
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath endswith ".npmrc" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("whoami","publish","login") and FolderPath !contains @"\.ssh\")
Response runbook
1. Triage: list all credential-store paths the npm/node PID touched and the package owning the install (cwd → package.json); flag the package version in your npm registry's audit log. 2. Contain: rotate every credential the process had access to (SSH key, npm token via `npm token revoke`, AWS access keys, GitHub PATs); isolate the host. 3. Hunt: search DeviceNetworkEvents from same host ±10m of the file reads for outbound POSTs to github.com/api, gist.github.com, webhook.site or the IOC list (UC7) — that's the exfil channel.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileAccessed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\.ssh\", "/.ssh/", @"\.npmrc", "/.npmrc", @"\.aws\credentials", "/.aws/credentials", @"\.docker\config.json", "/.docker/config.json", "kubeconfig", "wallet.dat", "MetaMask", @"Local Storage\leveldb")
   or FileName in~ (".env",".npmrc","credentials","id_rsa","id_ed25519","config.json")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\node_modules\.bin\"  // skip self-package metadata
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\.ssh\", "/.ssh/", @"\.npmrc", "/.npmrc", @"\.aws\credentials", "/.aws/credentials", @"\.docker\config.json", "/.docker/config.json", "kubeconfig", "wallet.dat", "MetaMask")
   or TargetFileName in~ (".env",".npmrc","credentials","id_rsa","id_ed25519","config.json")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

node_modules postinstall writing to autostart / persistence paths AIInstallation High
Reviewer #4: a postinstall hook running with a node_modules cwd creates files in OS persistence locations (Run keys via reg writes, Startup folder, /etc/cron.d, ~/.bashrc, LaunchAgents). Detects the persistence stage when a postinstall payload tries to survive reboot. Rationale: Reviewer #4 grounded in article's claim that postinstall code 'runs it, and deletes itself' but also 'plenty of legitimate packages use install scripts for native builds AND SETUP'. Persistence writes from a node_modules context are extremely abnormal — typical install scripts touch the project tree, not OS autostart locations. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/003/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.003 T1546.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Electron app installers (electron-builder) legitimately writing to Startup or LaunchAgents during dev installs
  • asdf/nvm postinstall touching ~/.bashrc to add PATH lines
  • Homebrew formula linked via npm package writing to /usr/local
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("electron-builder","nvm-windows","asdf","electron-installer"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: read the actual file content written (or registry value data) — extract any command line, URL or hash; identify the npm package owning the postinstall via parent cwd. 2. Contain: remove the persistence artifact, kill any spawned child of it, isolate the host, and pull the package version from your private mirror. 3. Hunt: pivot the SHA256 of the written file and the RegistryValueData across the fleet; check the npm package's other recent versions for the same postinstall pattern.
let PersistenceFileWrites = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","postinstall","preinstall") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\", "/etc/cron.", "/etc/systemd/system/", "Library/LaunchAgents/", "Library/LaunchDaemons/")
       or FileName in~ (".bashrc",".bash_profile",".zshrc",".profile")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, SHA256;
let PersistenceRegWrites = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","postinstall","preinstall") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules"
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options", @"\Userinit")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData;
PersistenceFileWrites
| union PersistenceRegWrites
| order by Timestamp desc
let PersistenceFileWrites = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","bun.exe","sh","bash","powershell.exe","cmd.exe")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","postinstall","preinstall")
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\", "/etc/cron.", "/etc/systemd/system/", "Library/LaunchAgents/", "Library/LaunchDaemons/")
       or TargetFileName in~ (".bashrc",".bash_profile",".zshrc",".profile")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, SHA256;
let PersistenceRegWrites = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","postinstall","preinstall")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData;
PersistenceFileWrites
| union PersistenceRegWrites
| order by TimeGenerated desc

(#event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate)
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|bun|powershell|cmd)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/node_modules|postinstall|preinstall/i
| TargetFileName=/Startup\\|\/etc\/cron|\/etc\/systemd|\.bashrc$|\.zshrc$|LaunchAgents|LaunchDaemons/i OR RegObjectName=/CurrentVersion\\Run|RunOnce|Userinit/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, RegObjectName, RegStringValue], function=count())

package.json with postinstall containing curl/wget/powershell -enc or base64 written to disk AIDelivery Medium
Reviewer #5: catches the malicious manifest before/while it lands on a developer's box. Monitors writes of package.json files whose content contains a postinstall hook with high-risk commands (network download, encoded interpreter invocation, suspicious shell chains). High value as a pre-execution canary. Rationale: Reviewer #5 directly tied to article's central thesis (postinstall in package.json is the attack vector). Pure file-create surfacing on its own is noisy — the rule's value is feeding content-scan logic (DLP / custom file-content rule) that hits on the manifest patterns described in the article (curl/wget download then run, base64 decode). Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Routine npm install creates 1000s of package.json files — without a content predicate, this is pure noise; rule is built to feed a DLP content scanner
  • Yarn workspaces rewriting package.json on dep changes
  • Internal package publishing pipelines
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the postinstall string from the written package.json; if it contains curl/wget/powershell -enc/base64 -d/bun.sh/install, escalate. 2. Contain: block the package name + version in your private npm registry and Safe Chain allowlist; revoke any cached install on dev boxes. 3. Hunt: search the org for every host that resolved the same package version (npm cache, package-lock.json commits in git); cross-check the maintainer's other published packages in the last 30 days for the same postinstall fingerprint.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has_any ("node_modules", "npm-cache", @"\AppData\Roaming\npm\")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
// Enrich with file-content scanning (DLP / Defender AV exclusion list query) for postinstall + (curl|wget|powershell -enc|base64 -d|bun.sh/install) substring matches — Advanced Hunting cannot read file content directly.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("node_modules", "npm-cache", @"\AppData\Roaming\npm\")
   or ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, SHA256, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: package.json Postinstall Hook Written to Disk
id: 4f2a09c2-7b5e-4c2d-93f1-6f1d8a2b5e91
description: Surfaces every npm/yarn/bun-driven write of package.json into node_modules or npm-cache for downstream content scanning (curl/wget/powershell -enc/bun.sh in postinstall).
references:

    TargetFilename|contains:

level: low

#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\node_modules\\.*\\package\.json$|\/node_modules\/.*\/package\.json$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|bun|yarn|pnpm)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
// Pair with a downstream content-scan workflow that greps the written file for /"(postinstall|preinstall)"\s*:\s*"[^"]*(curl|wget|powershell\s+-e|base64\s+-d|bun\.sh\/install)[^"]*"/
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="package.json" AND Filesystem.action="created" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner dest [ search index=files sourcetype=package_json ("postinstall" OR "preinstall") ("curl " OR "wget " OR "powershell -enc" OR "powershell -e " OR "base64 -d" OR "FromBase64String" OR "bun.sh/install" OR "github.com/oven-sh/bun" OR "| sh" OR "| bash") | rename host as dest | fields dest file_path raw_text ]
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="package.json" AND Filesystem.action="created" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner dest [ search index=files sourcetype=package_json ("postinstall" OR "preinstall") ("curl " OR "wget " OR "powershell -enc" OR "powershell -e " OR "base64 -d" OR "FromBase64String" OR "bun.sh/install" OR "github.com/oven-sh/bun" OR "| sh" OR "| bash") | rename host as dest | fields dest file_path raw_text ]
Cloud instance metadata service queried by Node/npm/Bun process AIActions on Objectives High
Detects cloud-credential theft by a postinstall payload running on a CI/build agent or developer cloud workstation. Node/npm/Bun reaching out to the AWS/Azure/GCP IMDS endpoint (169.254.169.254 or metadata.google.internal) during an install lifecycle is a high-fidelity supply-chain credential-access signal. Rationale: Article: 'payload scans for tokens, SSH keys, and other goodies' — on cloud-hosted CI runners and dev environments, IMDS is the highest-value token source (instance role creds with S3/secretsmanager access). Verified vs MITRE T1552.005. IMDS access does not surface in CloudTrail (it's a metadata-service local API), so cloudwatch_query left empty. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1078.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 doing credential resolution at app runtime on EC2 (not in install lifecycle — distinguish by parent chain)
  • Node app legitimately implementing IMDSv2 for instance role refresh
  • EKS pod's Node service using IRSA falling back to IMDS
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("@aws-sdk","aws-sdk-client") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has "node_modules\.bin")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm npm install lifecycle was active when IMDS was hit (parent chain → npm install / postinstall); capture the IAM role of the instance and what credentials would have been returned. 2. Contain: revoke the instance role's session via AWS STS / GCP service-account session revocation; isolate the host; rotate the role's permissions if STS credentials were retrieved. 3. Hunt: pivot in CloudTrail for the leaked role's AccessKeyId in the next 24h, look for unusual API activity (S3 list/get, secretsmanager get-secret-value, sts get-caller-identity from unfamiliar IPs); sweep the fleet for the same npm package version.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254","fd00:ec2::254") or RemoteUrl has_any ("metadata.google.internal","metadata.azure.com","169.254.169.254")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node_modules","bun install")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let ImdsTraffic = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254" or DstHostname has_any ("metadata.google.internal","metadata.azure.com")
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol;
let NpmProcesses = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
       or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node_modules","bun install")
    | project ProcessTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
ImdsTraffic
| join kind=inner NpmProcesses on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (ProcessTime .. ProcessTime + 5m)
| project NetTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by NetTime desc

id: 7d2cda4e-50e1-4f9f-9eaf-31a8e2a3b7c1
description: Node/npm/Bun process contacting AWS/Azure/GCP instance metadata service - postinstall cloud-credential theft from CI/build agents.

Outbound connection to known npm-supply-chain campaign IOCs from Node/npm/Bun AICommand & Control High
Hits the published IOCs tied to recent npm postinstall campaigns: 142.11.206.73, sfrclak.com, and webhook.site as a generic exfil sink. Pivots on the connection originating from a node/npm/bun process to anchor it to the supply-chain attack class rather than browsing or other webhook.site usage. Rationale: Pre-extracted campaign IOCs 142.11.206.73, sfrclak.com, webhook.site bound to npm/node/bun originator (article-thesis fingerprint). webhook.site is a known generic exfil sink in Shai-Hulud-style stealers. Cross-checked against abuse.ch threat-intel feeds and MITRE T1567 patterns. cloudwatch_query empty because these are endpoint outbound flows not CloudTrail events. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/ • https://threatfox.abuse.ch/ • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually testing webhook.site URL during Node app integration testing (low frequency; investigate parent chain)
  • Internal load-test or QA tool that POSTs to webhook.site from a Node test harness
Response runbook
1. Triage: capture the originating npm package + version from cwd, the exact URL path hit on webhook.site (the path is unique to the attacker's bucket — IOC-pivot), and any payload size. 2. Contain: block the IOCs at proxy/EDR network controls; isolate the host; revoke every cached credential on the box (npm token, GitHub PAT, AWS, GCP, SSH); pull the package version. 3. Hunt: pivot the destination URL path across the org (other hosts beaconing to the same webhook.site bucket = same compromise); query CloudTrail / Entra audit for use of any potentially-leaked tokens in the prior 7 days.
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["sfrclak.com","webhook.site"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where RemoteIP in (CampaignIPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node_modules")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignIPs = dynamic(["142.11.206.73"]);
let CampaignDomains = dynamic(["sfrclak.com","webhook.site"]);
let NetHits = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (CampaignIPs) or DstHostname in (CampaignDomains) or DstHostname endswith ".sfrclak.com" or DstHostname endswith ".webhook.site"
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber;
let NpmContext = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","bun.exe","bun","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
       or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm install","postinstall","preinstall","node_modules","bun install")
    | project ProcessTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
NetHits
| join kind=inner NpmContext on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (ProcessTime .. ProcessTime + 10m)
| project NetTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber
| order by NetTime desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    object payload signature.

            - '\mshta.exe'

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Unauthenticated POST /mcp Tool Invocation against Meta Ads MCP (CVE-2026-48039) AIExploitation Medium
Detects inbound HTTP POST requests to the vulnerable Meta Ads MCP `/mcp` endpoint on TCP 8080 from public sources hitting a python/uvicorn/gunicorn/docker listener. Targets the exact exploitation vector described in the GHSA PoC: AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch (http_auth_integration.py:272) accepts unauthenticated JSON-RPC `tools/call` requests and returns 200 OK with the operator's META_ACCESS_TOKEN leaked in the response body. Rationale: Anchors on the article's exact PoC: POST /mcp to localhost:8080 returning HTTP 200 with the MCP listener spawned by python/uvicorn/gunicorn/docker — all literal strings from `docker run -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ... meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the JSON-RPC body. Public-source restriction differentiates exploitation from legitimate internal MCP clients. No second source searched — GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr is itself the authoritative advisory.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized internal MCP clients invoking /mcp from corporate ranges (mitigated by RemoteIPType==Public filter)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) probing port 8080 during authorized scans
  • CI/CD pipeline running integration tests against a dev meta-ads-mcp instance from a hosted runner with a public egress IP
  • Other unrelated applications binding port 8080 (Tomcat, custom dashboards) — narrowed by InitiatingProcessFileName / module string filter
  • Reverse-proxy health probes from a managed cloud LB if the LB's NATed IP is not on the RFC1918 allowlist
Suppression filter
// Defender — exclude internal load-balancer health probes and authorized operator IPs
| where not(RemoteIP in ("10.0.0.1","corp-lb-egress-IP-here"))
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--health-check"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full HTTP request from the proxy/web log — confirm absence of Authorization or X-Auth-Token / X-Pipeboard-Token headers and verify the JSON-RPC body invokes a tools/call method (e.g. get_ad_accounts). Geo-locate the source IP and check against the authorized operator list. 2. Contain: Immediately rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN at https://developers.facebook.com (assume disclosure even if no error path was hit). Block the source IP at the edge, restrict /mcp to localhost or an internal VLAN via firewall rule, and patch beyond 1.0.105 once vendor confirms a tagged fix. 3. Hunt: Search proxy logs for any /mcp 200 responses whose body contains the literal string `access_token=` (UC 2 covers the network-level corroboration). Pivot on the source IP for follow-on direct calls to graph.facebook.com using the leaked credential in Meta's app audit logs.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ListeningConnectionCreated","ConnectionAccepted")
| where LocalPort == 8080
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn.exe","gunicorn","docker.exe","dockerd.exe","containerd.exe","node.exe","node")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","fastmcp","pipeboard")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalIP, LocalPort,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          CVE="CVE-2026-48039", Endpoint="POST /mcp (unauth tool invocation)"
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where DstPortNumber == 8080
| where HttpMethod == "POST"
| where (Url has "/mcp") or (UrlOriginal has "/mcp")
| where HttpStatusCode == 200
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr)
| where SrcIpAddr !startswith "10."
   and SrcIpAddr !startswith "192.168."
   and SrcIpAddr !startswith "127."
   and not(SrcIpAddr matches regex @"^172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])\.")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, HttpMethod, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| extend CVE="CVE-2026-48039", Note="Unauthenticated MCP tool invocation (meta-ads-mcp)"
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Unauthenticated POST /mcp Tool Invocation (CVE-2026-48039 Meta Ads MCP)
id: 4d2e1a8b-7c63-4d92-bf41-cve202648039
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to /mcp paths on TCP 8080 returning HTTP 200 — the exploitation pattern of CVE-2026-48039 in pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp (<=1.0.101), where AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch forwards unauthenticated requests to MCP tool handlers and leaks META_ACCESS_TOKEN in the response.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1190
    - cve.2026.48039
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-method: POST
        cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mcp'
        sc-status: 200
        s-port: 8080
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Authorized internal MCP clients calling /mcp from corporate network ranges (suppress via SrcIp allowlist)
    - Internal vulnerability scanners (Nessus / Qualys) probing port 8080
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\uvicorn.exe OR *\\gunicorn.exe) @CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *fastmcp* OR *pipeboard*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *fastmcp* OR *--port 8080* OR *--port=8080*) @process.name:(python OR python3 OR uvicorn OR gunicorn))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080 ConnectionDirection=1

| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)

Meta Access Token Leak: Graph API Outbound within 30s of Unauth /mcp POST AIActions on Objectives High
Correlates an unauthenticated inbound POST to /mcp on TCP 8080 with an outbound HTTPS call to graph.facebook.com from the same host within a 30-second window. This is the smoking-gun token-leak signature of CVE-2026-48039: the MCP tool handler invokes `make_api_request()`, which appends META_ACCESS_TOKEN as a URL query param (api.py:136) and returns the failing request URL verbatim to the unauthenticated caller. Rationale: Combines the two distinct article-specific behaviours from api.py:136 (META_ACCESS_TOKEN appended to graph.facebook.com URL) and http_auth_integration.py:272 (unauth /mcp accepts request). The 30-second window models the synchronous tool-handler -> Graph API call described in the PoC. No second source needed — both code paths are quoted verbatim in the GHSA advisory.
ATT&CKT1528 T1190
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized internal MCP user invokes /mcp from a corporate VPN exit with a public-presenting IP (suppress via known-good source IP list)
  • Cloud LB / WAF in front of the MCP server presents traffic with its own public IP, masking the real client — correlation still fires but attacker IP is the LB
  • Synthetic monitoring (Pingdom, Datadog Synthetics) hitting /mcp on a schedule from public probe IPs
  • First-run smoke test from a CI runner with public egress
  • Penetration test against the deployment during an authorized engagement
Suppression filter
// Defender — exclude known scheduled refresh jobs running as system service
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--scheduled-refresh"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm the inbound source IP is unknown / external / not on the authorized operator list. Verify the timing — a sub-5-second delay between the /mcp POST and the graph.facebook.com call is the strongest signal (legitimate background token refresh tasks do not follow inbound traffic). Pull the /mcp HTTP response body from the proxy and search for `access_token=` literal. 2. Contain: Treat the META_ACCESS_TOKEN as compromised: rotate it immediately at https://developers.facebook.com, invalidate the Meta app's existing user-access tokens, and require MFA on the operator account. Quarantine the MCP host pending package upgrade past 1.0.105. 3. Hunt: Search Meta Business Manager audit logs for unfamiliar source IPs / user agents calling Graph API endpoints with the rotated token's app ID. Pivot on the attacker source IP across all corporate egress proxies for additional reconnaissance against pipeboard / MCP-related hostnames.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSeconds = 30;
let Inbound = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionAccepted")
    | where LocalPort == 8080
    | where RemoteIPType == "Public"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn.exe","docker.exe")
       or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","fastmcp")
    | project InboundTimestamp = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AttackerIP = RemoteIP, MCPListenerCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com" or RemoteUrl has "graph.fb.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","fastmcp")
| join kind=inner Inbound on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (InboundTimestamp .. InboundTimestamp + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, InboundTimestamp)
| project InboundTimestamp, GraphCallTimestamp = Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName,
          AttackerIP, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
          MCPProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName, MCPProcessCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          CVE="CVE-2026-48039", Indicator="Token-leak correlation (unauth /mcp -> graph.facebook.com)"
| order by InboundTimestamp desc

| join kind=inner (Inbound | project-rename HostKey = DstIpAddr) on HostKey
| where TimeGenerated between (InboundTimestamp .. InboundTimestamp + WindowSeconds * 1s)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, InboundTimestamp)
| project InboundTimestamp, GraphCallTimestamp = TimeGenerated, DelaySec,
          AttackerIP, MCPHost = HostKey, GraphUrl = Url, GraphMethod = HttpMethod,
          CVE="CVE-2026-48039", Indicator="Token leak via Graph API URL query parameter"
| order by InboundTimestamp desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR nginx OR apache.access) (@DestinationHostname:graph.facebook.com OR @http.url_details.host:graph.facebook.com OR @network.destination.name:graph.facebook.com) (@ContextImageFileName:(*python* OR *uvicorn* OR *gunicorn*) OR @process.name:(python OR python3 OR uvicorn OR gunicorn) OR @CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *fastmcp*) OR @process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp* OR *fastmcp*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^graph\.(facebook|fb)\.com$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/(python|python3|uvicorn|gunicorn)(\.exe)?$/i
| join({
    #event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 LocalPort=8080 ConnectionDirection=1
    | NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
    | NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
    | NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
    | InboundTime := _time

| DelaySec := _time - InboundTime
| DelaySec >= 0

Vulnerable pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp Installation Discovery (<=1.0.101 / 1.0.102-1.0.105 unconfirmed) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for hosts running affected versions of the pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp Python package. Combines Defender TVM software inventory (when present), Defender vulnerability KB matches on CVE-2026-48039, and process command lines that load the meta_ads_mcp module via python/uvicorn/gunicorn/docker. Flags <=1.0.101 as vulnerable and 1.0.102-1.0.105 as unconfirmed patch status per the advisory. Rationale: Article specifies affected package `pip:meta-ads-mcp <= 1.0.108`, repo `pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp`, commits `496c988~7d14226`, and the caveat that `1.0.102-1.0.105 lack git tags`. Detection uses literal package names, parses the version string against the exact ranges in the advisory, and falls back to runtime detection where TVM inventory has not yet refreshed.
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Hosts already patched to a confirmed-safe version >1.0.105 — flagged as 'Check vendor' status, requires manual verification
  • Developer workstations with the package installed for local testing (not internet-exposed)
  • CI/CD build agents that pip-install meta-ads-mcp briefly during integration tests — short-lived processes
  • Sanctioned internal MCP deployment behind a strict authentication proxy (architecturally mitigated)
  • Mirror/proxy package repositories that cache meta-ads-mcp pip metadata
Suppression filter
// Exclude developer workstations from alerting tier — leave in hunting view
| where DeviceName !startswith "DEV-"
| where DeviceName !startswith "LAB-"
Response runbook
1. Triage: For each flagged host, run `pip show meta-ads-mcp` or check the lockfile to confirm exact installed version. Check whether the listener is bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 or 127.0.0.1:8080 — only the former is exploitable from outside the host. 2. Contain: For internet-exposed installations of <=1.0.101, immediately firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only and rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN. For 1.0.102-1.0.105, treat as vulnerable until vendor publishes a tagged release confirming the fix. 3. Hunt: Cross-reference flagged hosts with UC 1 / UC 2 outputs to determine whether exploitation has already occurred. Pull last 30 days of /mcp 200 responses and grep for `access_token=` strings indicating prior leaks.
let LookbackDays = 30d;
let ParseVersion = (v:string) {
    case(
        v matches regex @"^1\.0\.(\d+)$" and toint(extract(@"^1\.0\.(\d+)$",1,v)) <= 101, "Vulnerable (<=1.0.101)",
        v matches regex @"^1\.0\.(102|103|104|105)$", "Unconfirmed patch (1.0.102-1.0.105 lack git tags)",
        v matches regex @"^1\.0\.(\d+)$" and toint(extract(@"^1\.0\.(\d+)$",1,v)) >= 106, "Check vendor (>=1.0.106)",
        "Manual review"
    )
};
union isfuzzy=true
(
    DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp","meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads_mcp")
    | extend VulnStatus = ParseVersion(SoftwareVersion)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnStatus, Signal="TVM Inventory"
),
(
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-48039"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnStatus=strcat("CVE-2026-48039 / sev:",VulnerabilitySeverityLevel), Signal="Defender VulnDB"
),
(
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","python3.exe","uvicorn.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn.exe","gunicorn","docker.exe","dockerd.exe")
        or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python","python3","uvicorn.exe","gunicorn.exe","docker.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","fastmcp")
        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","fastmcp")
    | summarize Timestamp=max(Timestamp), SampleCmd=any(ProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName
    | extend OSPlatform="", SoftwareVendor="pipeboard-co", SoftwareName="meta-ads-mcp (runtime detection)", SoftwareVersion=tostring(SampleCmd), VulnStatus="Runtime listener detected — confirm pip show meta-ads-mcp", Signal="Process runtime"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnStatus, Signal
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 30d;
union isfuzzy=true
(
    DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where CveId == "CVE-2026-48039"
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, Status=strcat("CVE / sev:", VulnerabilitySeverityLevel), Signal="DefenderVulnDB"
),
(
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)([\\/])(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn|docker|dockerd)(\.exe)?$"
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","fastmcp")
    | summarize TimeGenerated=max(TimeGenerated), Cmd=any(ActingProcessCommandLine) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName
    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName=DvcHostname, SoftwareVendor="pipeboard-co", SoftwareName="meta-ads-mcp (runtime)", SoftwareVersion=Cmd, Status="Runtime detected — pip show meta-ads-mcp to confirm version", Signal="ProcessRuntime"
),
(
    SecurityEvent

    | where NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\(python3?|uvicorn|gunicorn|docker|dockerd)\.exe$"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","pipeboard","fastmcp")

    | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName=Computer, SoftwareVendor="pipeboard-co", SoftwareName="meta-ads-mcp (runtime via 4688)", SoftwareVersion=Cmd, Status="Runtime — confirm version", Signal="SecurityEvent4688"
)

CVE-2026-48039 PoC Execution Artifacts (poc.py, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO, localhost:8080/mcp) AIDelivery High
Detects execution of artifacts directly traceable to the public CVE-2026-48039 PoC: process command lines containing the literal demo token `FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`, the demo container image name `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001`, the vulnerable file `http_auth_integration.py` / `AuthInjectionMiddleware`, file events for `poc.py`, and curl/python requests targeting `127.0.0.1:8080/mcp` or `localhost:8080/mcp`. High-fidelity signal that someone is replaying the GHSA PoC on a corporate host. Rationale: Anchors on literal strings unique to the GHSA PoC: `FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789` (the demo token), `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` (the docker image tag in the PoC), `AuthInjectionMiddleware` / `http_auth_integration.py` (the vulnerable class and file at line 272), and the literal `127.0.0.1:8080/mcp` URL. These strings appear nowhere outside this exact advisory or its derivatives — near-zero benign occurrence expected.
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security researcher reproducing the PoC for validation in a sanctioned lab — confirm via asset tag / lab CIDR
  • Authorized penetration test referencing CVE-2026-48039 in command lines for documentation
  • Vendor's own regression harness re-running the PoC against patched builds (rare on customer endpoints)
  • Detection-engineering team copy/pasting query strings into a terminal for testing (matches the FAKE_TOKEN string)
  • Documentation / training material being demonstrated in a screen-recorded session
Suppression filter
// Defender — exclude sanctioned red-team / detection-engineering hosts
| where DeviceName !startswith "REDTEAM-"
| where DeviceName !startswith "DETENG-"
| where AccountName !in~ ("redteam-svc","deteng-research")
Response runbook
1. Triage: Identify the executing user and host. Check whether the user is on the security/red-team roster and whether the host is tagged as a lab / sandbox. Pull parent-process chain to determine the source — was poc.py downloaded from GitHub, written via VSCode, or pasted into a terminal. 2. Contain: If unsanctioned, isolate the host via Defender Live Response, collect memory + the actual poc.py contents, and disable the user account pending interview. Rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN on any reachable MCP servers the user could have targeted (lateral consequences). 3. Hunt: Pivot on user + host for additional CVE-2026-48039 indicators (UC 1 inbound, UC 2 graph.facebook.com correlation). Check egress proxy logs for the source host calling graph.facebook.com directly with a bearer token in URL or Authorization header in the last 30 days.

        or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO","meta-ads-mcp-vuln001")

id: a8e7d9c3-5f24-4b11-9a8c-cve202648039
status: experimental
description: Detects process command lines containing literal strings from the public CVE-2026-48039 PoC (FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789, meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 docker image, AuthInjectionMiddleware class, http_auth_integration.py source file) or direct python/curl/wget HTTP requests to 127.0.0.1:8080/mcp or localhost:8080/mcp — the canonical PoC replay pattern.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/18
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.006
    - attack.initial_access
    - attack.t1190
    - cve.2026.48039
logsource:
    category: process_creation
detection:
    selection_poc_literals:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO'
            - 'meta-ads-mcp-vuln001'
            - 'AuthInjectionMiddleware'
            - 'http_auth_integration.py'
    selection_mcp_endpoint:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '127.0.0.1:8080/mcp'
            - 'localhost:8080/mcp'
    condition: selection_poc_literals or selection_mcp_endpoint
falsepositives:
    - Authorized security researcher reproducing the PoC in an isolated lab
    - Sanctioned penetration test / red-team engagement
    - The vendor's own QA / regression harness exercising the patched fix
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @CommandLine:(*FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO* OR *meta-ads-mcp-vuln001* OR *AuthInjectionMiddleware* OR *http_auth_integration.py* OR *127.0.0.1\:8080/mcp* OR *localhost\:8080/mcp*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO* OR *meta-ads-mcp-vuln001* OR *AuthInjectionMiddleware* OR *http_auth_integration.py* OR *127.0.0.1\:8080/mcp* OR *localhost\:8080/mcp*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO|meta-ads-mcp-vuln001|AuthInjectionMiddleware|http_auth_integration\\.py|(127\\.0\\.0\\.1|localhost):8080/mcp", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function={ first := min(_time) | last := max(_time) | sample_cmd := any(CommandLine) })
ENDPOINT

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48039")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48039")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
